fn production() {}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    // assert_pos has a run of six assertions: assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!,
    // debug_assert!, std::assert! and debug_assert_eq!.
    #[test]
    fn assert_pos() {
        let got = production();
        assert!(got.is_ok());
        assert_eq!(got, 1);
        assert_ne!(got, 2);
        debug_assert!(got > 0);
        std::assert!(got < 9);
        debug_assert_eq!(got, 1);
        println!("not an assertion");
    }

    // assert_neg has two runs of five: the longest is 5.
    #[test]
    fn assert_neg() {
        assert!(a);
        assert!(b);
        assert!(c);
        assert!(d);
        assert!(e);
        println!("break");
        assert!(a);
        assert!(b);
        assert!(c);
        assert!(d);
        assert!(e);
    }

    // helper has no #[test]: not measured.
    fn helper() {
        assert!(a);
    }

    // dup_a and dup_b share four identical assertions.
    #[test]
    fn dup_a() {
        assert_eq!(got.a, 1);
        assert_eq!(got.b, 2);
        assert_eq!(got.c, 3);
        assert_eq!(got.d, 4);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn dup_b() {
        assert_eq!(got.a, 1);
        assert_eq!(got.b, 2);
        assert_eq!(got.c, 3);
        assert_eq!(got.d, 4);
        check();
    }

    // near_a and near_b share only three identical assertions.
    #[test]
    fn near_a() {
        assert_eq!(want.a, 1);
        assert_eq!(want.b, 2);
        assert_eq!(want.c, 3);
        assert_eq!(want.d, 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn near_b() {
        assert_eq!(want.a, 1);
        assert_eq!(want.b, 2);
        assert_eq!(want.c, 3);
        assert_eq!(want.e, 5);
    }
}
